Carmen (Support): @Josh saw your ticket about streaming dropping around 30s. Can you confirm client OS + proxy appliance?
Josh (Customer): Windows 10 + corporate 'BlueGate 5.2' proxy. Long responses cut off mid-stream. Users hit silence, then client reconnects and we see duplicate billing events.
Carmen (Support): Oof. Do you have a pcap or client console logs? Is proxy doing TLS inspect/terminate?
Josh (Customer): Proxy terminates TLS (MITM). Attaching a small tcpdump excerpt we grabbed from the edge:
```
12:01:23.451123 IP client > proxy: Flags [P.], seq 1:1450, ack 1, win 64240
12:01:23.451200 IP proxy > server: Flags [P.], seq 1:1450, ack 1, win 65535
12:01:51.472000 IP server > proxy: Flags [P.], seq 1450:2900, ack 1, win 65535
12:01:51.472100 IP proxy > client: Flags [.], ack 1450, win 64240
12:01:51.472200 IP client > proxy: Flags [R], seq 1450, ack 2900, win 0
```
Josh (Customer): The server sent payload (two segments) but proxy held it and only ACKed; client then RST after user reconnect.
Ben (Eng): That trace looks like PMTU/MSS fragmentation: first segment fits MTU, second crosses boundary and the proxy's reassembly/buffer triggers delayed push to client. Windows client then perceives a stall and RSTs.
Mina (Infra): We also see this when corporate proxies enable deep buffering for TLS-inspection. The combination: small MTU on the VPC link, proxy re-chunking, and Windows TCP delayed ACK/Nagle leads to a ~30s stall on heavy chunks.
Carmen (Support): Repro steps requested by engineering?
Ben (Eng): Minimal repro:
1) Run a curl streaming request from a Windows box behind the BlueGate proxy: `curl -N -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream`
2) Ask for a long generation (model: long-seq) so server sends multiple medium-sized SSE events; observe client silence ~25-35s.
3) On proxy capture: you should see server -> proxy pushes that are delayed until a fragmentation boundary, then client RST.
Carmen (Support): Any quick mitigation for customers?
Mina (Infra): Workarounds to propose:
- Configure proxy for TLS passthrough to avoid reassembly for streaming endpoints (if policy allows).
- Increase proxy max_buffer / disable re-chunking for SSE endpoints.
- Ensure PMTU discovery is correct on the VPC/private link; temporarily set MTU to 1400 on server/proxy to avoid fragmentation.
- Client-side: enable `TCP_NODELAY` or disable Nagle and set keepalive interval to <20s.
Ben (Eng): We can also add a server-side mitigation: send smaller initial chunks (<=1200B) while we triage. Quick patch: reduce SSE chunk size or insert periodic keepalive `:\n` lines every 10s so clients don't think the stream stalled.
Carmen (Support): @Josh can you try a quick workaround: 1) ask BlueGate team to enable passthrough for `/v1/stream` or bump buffer, OR 2) if admin can't change proxy, ask your app team to set `TCP_NODELAY` for the HTTP client and retry?
Josh (Customer): I'll try passthrough with infra team and report back. One more ask: what logs/traces should I send?
Ben (Eng): Please attach: ingress request-id (x-request-id), tcpdump snippet covering the stall, proxy logs around the session id, and a curl -v output. Also enable debug logging on the client side to capture socket state transitions.
Mina (Infra): Adding: if you can, run `sudo ip route get 8.8.8.8` on server/proxy to verify MTU and `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1` temporarily to test PMTU effects.
Carmen (Support): Thanks. I've opened an internal follow-up with eng and infra: we'll try the small-chunk server patch and confirm proxy adjustments. @Ben @Mina can you own triage?
Ben (Eng): On it. I'll prepare a small server patch to emit 1KB SSE chunks and add a keepalive line.
Mina (Infra): I'll coordinate with BlueGate support and check PMTU paths.
ingress-bot: session=0x1af3 info="keepalive sent" elapsed=00:00:30
Carmen (Support): Great — Josh, we'll circle back in this thread once we have a repro/pipeline of fixes. Please drop the artifacts requested when you have them. :thumbsup:
Josh (Customer): Thanks all, trying passthrough now, will update shortly.
